The conflict: axis "applicant": register says "Weber-Waagenbau u. Wägeelektronik GmbH", document says "Weber-Waagenbau und Wägeelektronik GmbH".

"u." is a German abbreviation for "und" (and). So these are spelling/abbreviation drift of the same company name — same-entity. Best value: which one? Rule says spelling drift = same-entity. The best_value should be the value the fused record should carry. For spelling drift, either is fine, but which is preferable? The rules explicitly specify best_value for document-noise (register), different-entity (document), and same-entity for number formats (register's canonical form). For name spelling drift under same-entity, no explicit rule on best_value. Reasonable: the register's canonical form is the database authority; but "und" is the expanded full form. Typically for fusion you'd pick the register's canonical form for consistency, unless the document is the legal instrument (only specified for different-entity). I'd pick the register form as canonical. But arguably the document's full spelled-out name is more complete. The rule structure: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." This suggests register is canonical authority generally. I'll go with register's canonical form "Weber-Waagenbau u. Wägeelektronik GmbH", noting "u." is standard abbreviation for "und".

Verdict: same-entity. One short sentence why.
